title: Scalar boundary propagation through general glancing
source_hypothesis: Arbitrary scalar smooth second-order operator with real quadratic principal symbol and noncharacteristic boundary, complex lower coefficients, actual intrinsic distributions and Dirichlet value data, in an open region avoiding both data fronts.
reviewed_arguments: C0 retains the full scalar second-order real principal symbol, a noncharacteristic smooth face, arbitrary complex lower coefficients, actual intrinsic distributions and Dirichlet traces. Indefinite or degenerate tangential forms are allowed.

C1 uses the boundary coordinate construction and exact normal gauge with every lower term. The first finite-order normal-recovery stage requires only the invertible normal coefficient. Its mixed weights and trace identities are explicitly checked.

C2 verifies tangential access to the zero of the normalized tangential symbol at every nonradial glancing point. The characteristic completion, full ordered quadratic array, normal commutator and actual Green boundary pairing then apply without a strict-diffraction sign assumption.

C3 proves the all-real regularized half-gain using actual H2 approximants and finite-order source pairings. The damping operator quantizes the chosen homogeneous frequency, not an unrelated Sobolev multiplier. All anti-Hermitian order-one terms cancel in the full characteristic array. A matching two-jet extension and explicit Fourier inequality recover the normal half-gain.

C4 uses only DC:T005 local smooth-flow construction, not its later Lorentz assumptions. The homogeneous clock, exact transverse invariants and defining-function bounds are uniform over compact glancing anchors.
C5 retains the signed normal term at both roots. The escape derivative is positive when delta is bounded by a fixed small multiple of epsilon, with constants independent of Sobolev order.

C6 constructs all flat smooth squares and a separate large parameter A at least 128 M delta. The characteristic square has a positive margin through root merging. Increasing the damping constant leaves every positivity set and incoming support unchanged.

C7 places the entire incoming symbol in the asserted enlarged window and uses the actual normal-frequency guard and fixed-collar smoothing theorem. Regularity at the window center alone is not substituted for regularity on its support.

C8 gives a finite sequence of nested supports for each requested gain while keeping the same final region for every order. The full equation and its differentiated Leibniz identities supply every normal derivative and actual boundary smoothness.

C9 verifies both signed time directions, the quantitative width-step relation and compact-uniform constants. Conjugation retains all lower coefficients and reverses the quadratic Hamilton orientation through the antipodal map. Quadratic-width witnesses give the precise geometric tangency hypothesis.

C10 checks the earlier interior, reflected and strict-diffractive segments for the same general scalar solution and data, then applies the complete closed-set construction. Radial and stationary normalized arcs are retained explicitly.

C11 proves continuation at finite compact endpoints with the actual joining derivative. It uses the finite-parameter part of the earlier maximal-extension construction and makes no infinite-parameter compact-escape claim without a global clock.

The three solutions include an ultrahyperbolic signature-(2,2) example, the exact damping threshold and twenty half-steps on one region, and a singular radial Dirichlet distribution. The last solution proves dual membership and excludes compressed normal covectors using an explicit annihilating boundary-tangent operator.
